lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and planning: mapping a support network by role

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic mapping a support network by role task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner privately identifies, for each of five life-role categories, at least one real person in their life who could help, but records the map using only relationship or role labels (such as 'a school counselor' or 'an aunt') rather than full names, keeping the map for their own private reference.
safetyNotes: Full names, addresses, phone numbers, or other identifying details are never entered into this task sheet; use role/relationship labels only (e.g., 'a neighbor,' 'a school counselor').
If a category has no one the learner can think of, it is acceptable and useful information to record honestly as a gap rather than inventing a name.
This map is for the learner's own private reference; nothing here requires sharing who any specific person is with anyone else to complete the lesson.
materials: learner-local: paper or a private notes document
learner-local: the five provided role categories

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Now that this is written down, would you actually remember to use it in a real situation? What would help you remember?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Map completeness and honesty: All five categories have either a role label or an honest recorded gap. | Privacy discipline: Only role/relationship labels are used throughout, with no identifying details. | Actionable next step: Next step is a concrete, realistic action tied to the named gap. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a second person for each category where they could, so the map has a backup, not just a first choice, and write one sentence on why having a backup matters for at least one category.

resources.title: mapping a support network by role worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner privately identifies, for each of five life-role categories, at least one real person in their life who could help, but records the map using only relationship or role labels (such as 'a school counselor' or 'an aunt') rather than full names, keeping the map for their own private reference.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact mapping a support network by role decision or action.
Model move 2: Before mapping, think about the five categories: money questions, school/career questions, health questions, a big decision, and an emergency.
Model move 3: For each of the five categories, record a role/relationship label for someone you could ask, or record it honestly as a gap.

Model check: Map completeness and honesty: All five categories have either a role label or an honest recorded gap. | Privacy discipline: Only role/relationship labels are used throughout, with no identifying details. | Actionable next step: Next step is a concrete, realistic action tied to the named gap.

resources.title: mapping a support network by role action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for mapping a support network by role.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: mapping a support network by role coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner privately identifies, for each of five life-role categories, at least one real person in their life who could help, but records the map using only relationship or role labels (such as 'a school counselor' or 'an aunt') rather than full names, keeping the map for their own private reference.
Coach direction: Before mapping, think about the five categories: money questions, school/career questions, health questions, a big decision, and an emergency.
Learner prompt: Which of the five categories comes to mind fastest for you, and which feels hardest to think of someone for?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: mapping a support network by role complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each of the five categories, record a role/relationship label for someone you could ask, or record it honestly as a gap.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I filled in a role label or an honest 'no one yet' for the money-questions category.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I filled in a role label or an honest 'no one yet' for the school/career-questions category.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I filled in a role label or an honest 'no one yet' for the health-questions category.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I filled in a role label or an honest 'no one yet' for the big-decision and emergency categories.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: mapping a support network by role minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Now that this is written down, would you actually remember to use it in a real situation? What would help you remember?

Success checks: Map completeness and honesty: All five categories have either a role label or an honest recorded gap. | Privacy discipline: Only role/relationship labels are used throughout, with no identifying details. | Actionable next step: Next step is a concrete, realistic action tied to the named gap.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: mapping a support network by role supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional mapping a support network by role condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Map completeness and honesty: All five categories have either a role label or an honest recorded gap. | Privacy discipline: Only role/relationship labels are used throughout, with no identifying details. | Actionable next step: Next step is a concrete, realistic action tied to the named gap..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
